cases.query: How do GraphRAG and REALM each use the notion of model performance to guide retrieval or evaluation in their respective approaches?
cases.reference_answer: GraphRAG employs an LLM-as-a-judge technique where one LLM generates diverse global sensemaking questions and a second LLM judges the answers of two RAG systems using predefined criteria, enabling comparison without ground-truth answers. REALM trains its retriever using a performance-based signal from unsupervised text, rewarding retrievals that improve the language model’s perplexity and penalizing uninformative ones, thereby optimizing the end-to-end retrieval-augmented prediction.
